prompt: When does a Developer become the sole owner of an item on the Sprint Backlog?

options.text: Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
At the Sprint Planning event.
During the Daily Scrum.
Never. All items in the Sprint Backlog are "owned" by the Developers on the Scrum Team.

explanation: The Sprint Backlog is updated by the Developers throughout the Sprint as more is learned.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Backlog (owned by Developers; plan by and for Developers).

prompt: Who has the final say on the order of the Product Backlog?

options.text: The Stakeholders.
The Product Owner.
The Developers.
The Scrum Master.
The CEO.

explanation: The Product Owner is the sole person responsible for ordering the Product Backlog.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Owner (ordering the Product Backlog).

prompt: Why is the Daily Scrum held at the same time and same place?

options.text: Rooms are hard to book and this lets it be booked in advance.
The place can be named.
The Product Owner demands it.
The consistency reduces complexity.

explanation: The Daily Scrum is held at the same time and place each day to reduce complexity.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum (reduce complexity through consistency).

prompt: Who is required to attend the Daily Scrum?

options.text: The Developers and Product Owner.
The Scrum Master and Product Owner.
The Developers and Scrum Master.
The Scrum Team.
The Developers.

explanation: …they will need to be at the Daily Scrum.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum (event for Developers).

prompt: When does the next Sprint begin?

options.text: Next Monday.
Immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint.
Immediately following the next Sprint Planning.
When the Product Owner is ready.

explanation: A new Sprint starts immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints (a new Sprint starts immediately after the previous one).

prompt: Which of the following are examples of a Scrum Team practicing Scrum poorly or not exhibiting traits of a self-managing Scrum Team?

options.text: The Developers invite external stakeholders to the Sprint Planning to ask them how to turn a Product Backlog item into an Increment via a complete and detailed Sprint Backlog.
The Developers have all the skills they need to create a valuable, useful Increment.
The Developers create their own Sprint Backlog, reflecting all work that is required to meet the Definition of Done.
Stakeholders attend the Daily Scrum to check on the Scrum Team’s progress.
The Developers are working within the boundaries of their organization's functional description and nicely handing off work from analyst to developer to tester to integration.
The Developers are collaboratively selecting their own work during the Sprint.

explanation: Accountability belongs with the Scrum Team as a whole, regardless of whether team members have specialized skills.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team (no sub-teams/titles; self-managing, cross-functional).

prompt: The Product Backlog is ordered by:

options.text: Least valuable items at the top to most valuable at the bottom.
Items are randomly arranged.
Size, where small items are at the top and large items are at the bottom.
Risk, where safer items are at the top, and riskier items are at the bottom.
Whatever is deemed most appropriate by the Product Owner.

explanation: It is the single source of work undertaken by the Scrum Team.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog (emergent, ordered list; PO accountable).

prompt: What is the main reason for the Scrum Master to be at the Daily Scrum?

options.text: To write down any changes to the Sprint Backlog, including adding new items, and tracking progress on the burn-down.
To gather status and progress information to report to management.
To make sure every team member answers the three questions.
They do not have to be there; they only need to ensure the Developers have a Daily Scrum.

explanation: The Scrum Master only ensures that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master (ensures events occur and are effective).

prompt: Which of the following services is appropriate for a Scrum Master in regard to the Daily Scrum?

options.text: Lead the discussions of the Developers.
Ensure that all 3 questions have been answered.
Facilitate in a way that ensures each team member has a chance to speak.
Teach the Developers to keep the Daily Scrum within the 15 minute timebox.
All answers apply.

explanation: The Scrum Master enforces the rule that only Developers participate in the Daily Scrum.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum (timebox) & Scrum Master as teacher/coach.

prompt: When might a Sprint be cancelled?

options.text: When the sales department has an important new opportunity.
When it becomes clear that not everything will be finished by the end of the Sprint.
When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
When the Developers feel that the work is too hard.

explanation: A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel the Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Cancelling a Sprint (PO authority; obsolete Sprint Goal).

prompt: Who creates the Definition of Done?

options.text: If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done appropriate for the product.
The Scrum Master since they are responsible for the productivity of the Developers.
The Scrum Team, in a collaborative effort where the result is the common denominator of all members' definitions.
The Product Owner since they are responsible for the product's success.

explanation: If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done appropriate for the product.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done (organizational standards vs team).

prompt: Which statement best describes the Sprint Review?

options.text: It is when the Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the outcome of a Sprint and figure out what to do next.
It is a mechanism to control Developer activity during a Sprint.
It is a demo at the end of the Sprint for everyone in the organization to check on the work done.

explanation: Every event in Scrum, besides the Sprint, which is a container for the other events, is an opportunity to Inspect and Adapt.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Review (inspect outcomes; adapt).

prompt: The timebox for a Daily Scrum is?

options.text: 15 minutes.
15 minutes for a 4-week sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
4 hours.
Two minutes per person.
The same time of day every day.

explanation: Because it is a short event, the timebox is not influenced by the Sprint length.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum (15-minute event).

prompt: When does a Sprint conclude?

options.text: When the Product Owner decides enough has been delivered to meet the Sprint Goal.
When the Sprint Retrospective is complete.
When all the tasks are completed by the Developers.
When all Product Backlog items meet their Definition of Done.

explanation: Only the Product Owner has the authority to end the Sprint prematurely.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints (fixed length; Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint).

prompt: The Developers should not be interrupted during the Sprint and the Sprint Goal should remain intact. Which one of the following answers is FALSE?

options.text: The Product Owner can help clarify or optimize the Sprint when asked by the Developers.
The Developers may work with the Product Owner to add or remove work if they find themselves with more or less capacity than expected.
The Sprint Backlog is fully formulated in the Sprint Planning event and does not change during the Sprint.
As a decomposition of the selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Backlog changes and may grow as the work emerges.

explanation: The Developers modify the Sprint Backlog throughout the Sprint, and the Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Backlog (emerges; updated throughout the Sprint).

prompt: Which statement best describes Scrum?

options.text: A framework for creating complex products in complex environments.
A complete methodology that defines how to develop software.
A cookbook that defines best practices for software development.
A defined and predictive process that conforms to the principles of Scientific Management.

explanation: Scrum is a lightweight framework that helps people, teams and organizations generate value through adaptive solutions for complex problems.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — What is Scrum? (lightweight framework; complex problems).

prompt: The three pillars of Scrum are:

options.text: Transparency, Inspection, Adaptation.
Planning, Inspection, Adaptation.
Respect For People, Kaizen, Eliminating Waste.
Planning, Demonstration, Retrospective.
Transparency, Eliminating Waste, Kaizen.

explanation: The three pillars uphold empirical and lean thinking: transparency, inspection, and adaptation.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Theory (pillars of empiricism).

prompt: When many Scrum Teams are working on a single product, what best describes the Definition of Done?

options.text: All Scrum Teams must have a Definition of Done that makes their combined Increment valuable and useful.
It depends.
Each Scrum Team uses its own, but must make their definition clear to all other teams so the differences are known.

explanation: This means that when many Scrum Teams are working on a single product, they are expected to adhere to a single Definition of Done for the Increment.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Definition of Done (single DoD for a product).

prompt: The timebox for the Sprint Review is:

options.text: 1 day.
2 hours.
As long as needed.
4 hours and longer as needed.
4 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.

explanation: For shorter Sprints, the event is usually shorter.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Review (≤4h for one-month Sprint).

prompt: An organization has decided to adopt Scrum, but management wants to change the terminology to fit with terminology already used. What will likely happen if this is done?

options.text: Without a new vocabulary as a reminder of the change, very little change may actually happen.
The organization may not understand what has changed with Scrum and the benefits of Scrum may be lost.
Management may feel less anxious.
All of the above.

prompt: During a Sprint, a Developer determines that the Scrum Team will not be able to complete the items in their forecast. Who should be present to review and adjust the Product Backlog items selected?

options.text: The Product Owner and the Developers.
The Scrum Master, the project manager, and the Developers.
The Product Owner and all stakeholders.
The Developers.

explanation: …ultimately the entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — During Sprint: PO and Developers can re-negotiate scope.

prompt: Who should know the most about the progress toward a business objective or a release, and be able to explain the alternatives most clearly?

options.text: The Scrum Master
The Product Owner
The Developers
The Project Manager

explanation: …ensuring that the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Owner accountabilities.

prompt: What should the Scrum Team do during the first Sprint?

options.text: Create the complete Product Backlog to be developed in subsequent Sprints.
Develop a plan for the rest of the release.
Determine the complete architecture and infrastructure for the product.
Create a valuable and useful Increment.

explanation: This applies to every Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints (each Sprint creates a valuable, useful Increment).

prompt: The Developers should have all the skills needed to:

options.text: Complete the project as estimated when the date and cost are committed to the Product Owner.
Do all of the development work, except for specialized testing that requires additional tools and environments.
Turn the Product Backlog items they select into an Increment of a useful and valuable product.

explanation: As a team, Developers have all of the skills necessary to create a product Increment.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team is cross-functional; Developers create the Increment.

prompt: True or False: When multiple Scrum Teams work together on the same product, each team should maintain a separate Product Backlog.

options.text: True
False

explanation: Products have one Product Backlog, regardless of how many Scrum Teams are used.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Backlog (single backlog per product).

prompt: True or False: Scrum has a role called "project manager."

options.text: True
False

explanation: A Scrum Team has a Scrum Master, a Product Owner and Developers.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team roles.

prompt: True or False: It is mandatory that the product Increment be released to production at the end of each Sprint.

options.text: True
False

explanation: The product Increment should be usable at the end of every Sprint, but it does not have to be released.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Increment (may be released at any time).

prompt: When should a Developer on a Scrum Team be replaced?

options.text: As needed, while taking into account a short-term reduction in productivity.
Every Sprint to promote shared learning.
As needed, with no special allowance for changes in productivity.
Never, it reduces productivity.

explanation: Changing membership typically reduces cohesion, affecting performance and productivity in the short term.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team (stable teams improve performance).

prompt: True or False: The purpose of a Sprint is to produce a valuable and useful Increment of a usable product.

options.text: True
False

explanation: …a timebox of one month or less during which a done, useful, and valuable working product Increment is created.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints (purpose and outcome).

prompt: What are two ways a Scrum Master serves to enable effective Scrum Teams?

options.text: By facilitating Developer decision-making.
By keeping high value features high in the Product Backlog.
By removing impediments that hinder the Scrum Team.
By starting and ending the meetings at the proper time.

explanation: Facilitation and removing impediments are examples of ways a Scrum Master helps a team become more effective.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Master (service to the Scrum Team).

prompt: How much work must the Developers complete for each Sprint?

options.text: All development work and at least some testing.
Enough so that the Increment meets the Definition of Done.
As much as it can fit into the Sprint.
Analysis, design, programming, testing and documentation.

explanation: The purpose of each Sprint is to deliver useful and valuable Increments that adhere to the Scrum Team's current Definition of Done.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints & Definition of Done.

prompt: The CEO asks the Developers to add a "very important" item to a Sprint that is in progress. What should the Developers do?

options.text: Add the item to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint.
Add the item to the current Sprint Backlog and do whatever amount of work is necessary to meet the Sprint Goal while satisfying the CEO.
Discuss the item with the other members of the Scrum Team so the team can decide what to do.
Add the item to the current Sprint Backlog, drop an item of similar size, and reduce the Sprint Goal.

explanation: No one external to the Scrum Team can force changes on the Developers.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Goal focus; Sprint Backlog owned by Developers.

prompt: The length of a Sprint should be:

options.text: Short enough to keep the business risk acceptable to the Product Owner.
Short enough to be able to synchronize the development work with other business events.
One month or less.
All of the above.

explanation: All of these choices are appropriate considerations in determining the length of a Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprints (length considerations).

prompt: Who is responsible for managing the progress of work during a Sprint?

options.text: The Product Owner.
The most junior member of the team.
The Developers.
The Scrum Master.

explanation: The Developers use the Daily Scrum to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and to inspect how progress is trending toward completing the work in the Sprint Backlog.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Daily Scrum (inspect progress toward Sprint Goal).

prompt: What is the function or purpose of Management in Scrum?

options.text: Continually monitor staffing levels of the Scrum Team.
Identify and remove people that are not working hard enough.
Monitor the progress of the Developers on the Scrum Team.

Support the Product Owner with insights and information into high value product and system capabilities. Support the Scrum Master to encourage organizational change that fosters empiricism, self-management, bottom-up intelligence, and intelligent product delivery.

explanation: Management has no official role or accountability on a Scrum Team.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team (accountabilities) & organizational support.

prompt: Who is on the Scrum Team?

options.text: Project Manager.
Developers.
The Product Owner.
The Scrum Master.

explanation: The Scrum Team consists of the Scrum Master, the Product Owner and Developers.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team composition.

prompt: What are three incorrect, untrue, or misleading statements about Scrum?

options.text: Scrum is a framework for developing and sustaining complex products.
Scrum is founded on empiricism and lean thinking.
Each component of Scrum serves a specific purpose and is essential to your ability to use Scrum to develop complex products.
Scrum is a methodology where you can pick and choose which parts of Scrum you think will work for your environment.
Scrum is a framework that eliminates complexity.
Scrum is like traditional processes but with self-organization to replace Project Managers.

explanation: Project Managers are not simply replaced by self-managing teams.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum is a framework; immutable elements; complexity remains.

prompt: The timebox for the Sprint Planning event is?

options.text: Monthly.
Whenever it is done.
8 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
4 hours.

explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to a maximum of eight hours for a one-month Sprint. For shorter Sprints, the event is usually shorter.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Planning (≤8h for one-month Sprint).

prompt: A Scrum Team consists of the following:

options.text: Customers
Product Owner
Developers
Users
Scrum Master

explanation: The Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner, and Developers.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team composition.

prompt: What does it mean to say that an event has a timebox?

options.text: The event can take no more than a maximum amount of time.
The event must happen at a set time.
The event must take at least a minimum amount of time.
The event must happen by a given time.

explanation: Timeboxed events are events that have a maximum duration.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Events (timeboxes).

prompt: Which statement best describes a Product Owner's responsibility?

options.text: Directing the Developers.
Maximizing the value of the work the Scrum Team does.
Managing the project and ensuring that the work meets the commitments to the stakeholders.
Keep stakeholders from distracting the Developers.

explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product and the work of the Scrum Team.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Product Owner accountability.

prompt: True or False: The Scrum Team must choose at least one high priority process improvement item, identified during the Sprint Retrospective, and place it in the Sprint Backlog.

options.text: True
False

explanation: It is simply not prescribed anymore, but can still be valuable.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Sprint Retrospective (2020 update removed the mandatory improvement item).

prompt: When does a Developer become accountable for the value of a Product Backlog item selected for the Sprint?

options.text: Never. The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating value every Sprint.
At the Sprint Planning Event.
Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
During the Daily Scrum.

explanation: All members of the Scrum Team share in the accountability for creating value every Sprint.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team accountability for value.

prompt: Which Scrum events are timeboxed?

options.text: Sprint Retrospective.
Sprint Planning.
Sprint Review.
Sprint Testing.
Release Testing.
Release Retrospective.
Refinement.

explanation: The Scrum Guide states that the Sprint Planning, Sprint Retrospectives, and Sprint Reviews are timeboxed events.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Events (timeboxes).

prompt: What is the typical size for a Scrum Team?

options.text: 7 plus or minus 2.
10 or fewer.
Minimum of 7.

explanation: A Scrum Team is small enough to remain nimble and large enough to complete significant work within a Sprint, typically 10 or fewer people.
source: Scrum Guide 2020 — Scrum Team size (typically 10 or fewer).
